rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars are blotted from their light and whiteness into blackness.
rows.anchor: بعد الضوء والبياض إلى السواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky opens so its angels descend, together with the Lord of Might, for the creatures’ reckoning.
rows.anchor: انفرجت عن نزول من فيها من الملائكة، ورب العزة لحساب الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are uprooted until level with the earth, as they were at first.
rows.anchor: من أصلها حتى استوت بالأرض، كما كانت أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers are gathered.
rows.anchor: يقول: جمعت، ثم رجع إلى الساعة في التقديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed day is the Hour, that is, the Day of Resurrection, when the angels are gathered.
rows.anchor: لأي يوم أجلها يعني الساعة يوم القيامة، وجمع الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision means the day of judgment.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم القضاء { ومآ أدراك ما يوم الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies the severity of that day, which the deniers reject.
rows.anchor: ماهو؟ تعظيما لشدتها فكذبوا بذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened deniers are those who reject resurrection.
rows.anchor: بالبعث، فقال: يا محمد { ألم نهلك الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed earlier peoples who denied the Resurrection with a blast, sinking, metamorphosis, division, and enmity.
rows.anchor: أهلكتهم بالصيحة والخسف والمسخ والفرق والعدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later people followed the earlier ones in destruction; these are Meccan unbelievers who rejected Muhammad.
rows.anchor: بالأولين بالهلاك يعني العذاب يعني كفار مكة لما كذبوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals means unbelieving wrongdoers; Meccans are warned not to reject Muhammad lest they suffer the earlier peoples’ fate.
rows.anchor: هكذا نفعل بالمجرمين يعني الكفار الظلمة، يخوف كفار مكة لئلا يكذبوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers threatened here are those who deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: { ويل يومئذ للمكذبين } [آية: 19] بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being is created from weak water, meaning semen; this beginning should make deniers reflect.
rows.anchor: يقول: ماء ضعيف وهو النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is lodged securely in the womb.
rows.anchor: يعني الماء يمكن في الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known term is nine months.
rows.anchor: { إلى قدر معلوم } [آية: 22] يعني تسعة أشهر { فقدرنا } الصبي في رحم أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God determines the child’s gestation as nine months, or a shorter or longer period.
rows.anchor: الصبي في رحم أمه تسعة أشهر، ودون ذلك أو فوق ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains that look stationary from afar turn first to molten matter, then teased wool, and finally vanish as a mirage; touching them reveals nothing.
rows.anchor: يعني من بعيد يحسبها جبلا قائما، فإذا انتهى إليه ومسه لم يجده شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are severed by fear of God on the Resurrection Day and become a mirage.
rows.anchor: فكانت سرابا فما حالك يا بن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressors are unbelievers, and their return is to Hell; the verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: يعني الكافرين { مآبا } [آية: 22] يعني المشركين مرجعا إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil reports that this passage was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: يعني المشركين مرجعا إليها نزلتفي الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers remain in Hell through epochs; Muqatil says there are seventeen, but their number and end are known only to God, with each epoch lasting eighty years, each year 360 days, and each day equivalent to a thousand years.
rows.anchor: أحقابا وهى سبعة عشر حقبا، يعني الأزمنة والأحقاب لا يدرى عددها، ولا يعلم منتهاهه إلا الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They taste no cooling like camphor, nor a cold, beneficial drink or pleasant refreshment; their drink is not the wine of Paradise.
rows.anchor: في تلك الأحقاب { بردا } يعني برد الكافور { ولا شرابا } [آية: 24] يعني الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil reports an unnamed gloss that al-bard means daytime.
rows.anchor: ويقال: البرد: اليوم

rows.speaker: أبو العباس أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: Al-Abbas glosses ḥamīm as molten liquid at extreme heat and ghassāq as extreme cold, the freezing zamharīr.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العباس أحمد بن يحيى ويقال: البرد: اليوم، { إلا حميما } يعني بالحميم المذاب الذي قد انتهى حره، { وغساقا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment corresponds to the crime: shirk is the worst deed, and fire is the worst punishment.
rows.anchor: كما أنه ليسفي الأعمال أخبث من الشرك بالله عز وجل وكذلكم ليس من العذاب شىء أخبث من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not fear being called to account for their wicked deeds.
rows.anchor: يعني أنهم كانوا لا يخافون من العذاب أن يحاسبوا بأعمالهم الخبيثة إذا عملوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs mean the Qur’an, and their denial rejects its commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن { كذابا } [آية: 28] يعني تكذيبا بما فيه من الأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All their deeds are recorded in a guarded book, the Preserved Tablet; Muqatil links this to the statement in Yā Sīn.
rows.anchor: من الأعمال { كتابا } [آية: 29] يعني ثبتناه مكتوبا عندنا في كتاب حفيظ يعني اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the blind man as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Musraḥ al-Aʿmar, also called Umm Maktūm’s son ʿAmr ibn Qays, and gives their lineages. While the blind man sat alone in the Sacred Mosque, two angels descended to pray; he heard one remark that Abū Ṭālib called people to Islam without seeing them. He then sought repentance from Muhammad, who turned back to al-ʿAbbās and Umayya ibn Khalaf; after the man repeated his plea and left despairing, these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي مسرح الأعمر، وأمه أم مكتوم، اسمه عمرو بن قيس بن زائدة بن رواحة بن الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet grimaced and turned away.
rows.anchor: يعني كلح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet turned away because the blind man came to him.
rows.anchor: { أن جآءه الأعمى } [آية: 2]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man might believe and pray, being reminded in the Qur’an of what he had corrupted.
rows.anchor: يقول: لعله أن يؤمن فيصلى فيتذكر في القرآن بما قد أفسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is an admonition: if Islam is presented to him and he believes, it will benefit him.
rows.anchor: يعني الموعظة، يقول: أن تعرض عليه الإسلام فيؤمن فتنفعه تلك الذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who considers himself self-sufficient from God is Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: عن الله في نفسه يعني أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet turns toward the self-sufficient man and invites him.
rows.anchor: يعني تدعو وتقبل بوجهك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not responsible if that man does not believe or mend what he corrupted; Muqatil applies this to the group of men.
rows.anchor: وما عليك ألا يؤمن ولا يصلح ما قد أفسد، هؤلاء النفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who comes striving in the heat and fears God is Ibn Umm Maktūm.
rows.anchor: في الحر { وهو يخشى } [آية: 9] الله يعني بن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet turns his face away from Ibn Umm Maktūm.
rows.anchor: يعني تعرض بوجهك عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God admonishes the Prophet to stop attending to those who feel self-sufficient and to welcome, rather than turn from, the person who comes fearing his Lord.
rows.anchor: لا تقبل عليه ولا تعرض عن من جاءك يسعى، ولا تقبل على من استغنى وتعرض عن من يخشى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the revelation concerning Ibn Umm Maktūm, the Prophet honored him and appointed him deputy over Medina twice during military expeditions.
rows.anchor: أكرمه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم واستخلفه بعد ذلك على المدينة مرتين في غزواته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is the Qur’an’s verses.
rows.anchor: يعني آيات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says God Himself makes the Qur’an understood, and says that whoever wills may remember, assigning the matter to servants.
rows.anchor: يعني الرب تعالى نفسه، يقول: من شاء الله تعالى فهمه يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The honored pages are honored books.
rows.anchor: يعني في كتب مكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised pages are the Preserved Tablet, elevated above the fourth heaven; they are purified of shirk and unbelief.
rows.anchor: يعني به اللوح المحفوظ، مرفوعة فوق السماء الرابعة نظيرها، في الواقعة عند الله { مطهرة } [آية: 14] من الشرك والكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pages are in the hands of noble, Muslim scribes.
rows.anchor: يعني تلك الصحف بأيدي كتبة كرام مسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scribes are angels: karām means Muslims, and barara means obedient to God, pure, righteous, and free of sins.
rows.anchor: يعني مسلمين، وهم الملائكة { بررة } [آية: 16] يعني مطيعين لله تعالى أنقياء أبرار من الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Night of Decree, the Preserved Tablet descends to the scribal angels in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brings it to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وكان ينزل إليهم اللوح المحفوظ إلى سماء الدنيا في ليلة القدر، إلى الكتبة من الملائكة، ثم ينزل به جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutila means the human is cursed; the verse refers to the person who disbelieved.
rows.anchor: يعني لعن الإنسان { مآ أكفره } [آية: 17] يقول: الذي أكفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab: after becoming Muslim during a dispute with his father, he reconciled with him and was sent to Syria for trade, then sent Muhammad word that he had rejected the Star. Muhammad prayed for a beast to devour him, and a lion ate him when he stopped on the road.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في عتبة بن أبى لهب بن عبدالمطلب، وذلك أنه كان غضب على أبيه فأتى محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فآمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains the human’s creation so that he will reflect on it.
rows.anchor: فأعلمه كيف خلقه ليعتبر في خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The embryo develops in the womb from a drop to a clot, then a lump, bones, and finally a spirit; God determines its form before birth.
rows.anchor: في بطن أمه من نطفة، ثم من عقلة، ثم من مضغة، ثم عظما، ثم روحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eases the way out of the mother’s womb; the human should reflect, affirm God’s oneness, and thank Him for His blessings and good creation.
rows.anchor: يعني هون طريقه في الخروج من بطن أمه يقول يسره للخروج أفلا يعتبر فيوحد الله في حسن خلقه فيشكر الله في نعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes the human to die at his appointed term and places him in a grave.
rows.anchor: عند أجله { فأقبره }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills, He resurrects the human after death.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة يعني إذا شاء بعثه من بعد موته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human does not believe in resurrection; Muqatil takes the unfulfilled command as the first covenant, namely monotheism, addressed to Adam.
rows.anchor: لا يؤمن الإنسان بالنشور، ثم استأنف فقال: { لما يقض مآ أمره } [آية: 23] يعني ما عهد الله إليه أمر الميثاق الأول، يعني التوحيد، يعني بها آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil then resumes by mentioning what the human was created for and the provision that should prompt reflection.
rows.anchor: ثم استأنف ذكر ما خلق عليه، فذكر رزقه ليعتبر

words: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلْكَرِيمِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Abū al-Ashaddayn, named Asīd ibn Kilda, a one-eyed man of great strength. He boasted that if he held the handle of Paradise’s gate, many people would enter; he was killed at the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبى الأشدين، أسمه أسيد بن كلدة، وكان أعور شديد البطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is what deluded the human being.
rows.anchor: يعني غره الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created, proportioned, and set the human upright.
rows.anchor: يعني فقومك

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assembled the human in whatever form He willed; He could have made him in a form other than human.
rows.anchor: يعني لو شاء ركبك في غير صورة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human does not believe in the One who created and shaped him; “the religion” here means the reckoning.
rows.anchor: لا يؤمن هذا الإنسان بمن خلقه وصوره، ثم قال: { بل تكذبون بالدين } [آية: 9] يعني الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians are angels who write the good and evil deeds of the children of Adam.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة يحفظون أعمالكم ثم نعتهم، فقال: { كراما } يعني مسلمين { كاتبين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels write people’s deeds in Syriac, whatever language a person speaks; reckoning is in Syriac, while on entering they speak Arabic in Muhammad’s language.
rows.anchor: يكتبون أعمال بنى آدم بالسريانية، فبأى لسان تكلم ابن آدم؟ فإنه إنما يكتبونه بالسريانية والحساب بالسريانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels know and record the human’s good and evil deeds.
rows.anchor: من الخير والشر فيكتبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are those who obey God in worldly life, and they will be in the bliss of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني المطيعين لله في الدنيا { لفي نعيم } [آية: 13] يعني نعيم الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record of the righteous is in Illiyīn, at the trunk of the Throne; it means the believers’ deeds and good works.
rows.anchor: لفي ساق العرش، يعني أعمال المؤمنين وحسناتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies the greatness of Illiyīn.
rows.anchor: ومآ أدراك ما عليون } [آية: 19] تعظيما لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is a book of good, sealed with mercy and recorded with God.
rows.anchor: يعني كتاب من كتب الخير مختوم ختم بالرحمة مكتوب عند الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses are angels, seven close angels from each heaven, who escort the deed God approves until it is fixed with Him, then return to their places.
rows.anchor: وهم الملائكة من كل سماء سعبة أملاك من مقربى أهل كل سماء يشيعون ذلك العمل الذي يرضاه الله حتى ثبوته عند الله جل وعز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are in the bliss of Paradise.
rows.anchor: يعني نعيم الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāʾik are the couches where the righteous sit looking at the bliss: a bed alone is a couch and a canopy alone is a canopy, while together they are arāʾik.
rows.anchor: فإذا اجتمع السرير والحجلة، فهى الأرائك يعني هؤلاء جلوس ينظرون إلى ذلك النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light of joy and bliss clings to their faces, making their happiness evident to anyone who looks at them.
rows.anchor: لأنه يعلق في وجهه النور من الفرح والنعيم، فلا يخفى عليك إذا نظرت إليهم فرحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sealed rāḥīq is white wine at its finest aroma; after drinking, the empty vessel leaves the taste of musk in the drinker’s mouth.
rows.anchor: وهو الخمر الأبيض إذا أنتهى طيبه { ختامه مسك } إذا شرب وفرغ ونزع الإناء من فيه وجد طعم المسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should compete and desire this reward.
rows.anchor: يعني فليتنازع المتنازعون، وفيه فليرغب الراغبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnim flows down from the Garden of Eden, described as Paradise’s core; the close ones of that garden drink wine mixed with its water. Muqatil also names al-Kawthar and al-Salsabīl.
rows.anchor: عينا } من جنة عدن، فتنصب عليم أنصبابا، فذلك قوله: { يشرب بها المقربون } [آية: 28] يقول: يشربون به الخمر

words: إن الذين أجرموا كانوا من الذين آمنوا يضحكون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and his companions. Hypocrites and Jews mocked and laughed at them as they passed on the way to the Prophet, including a joke about ʿAlī walking ahead of his companions. Abū Bakr was upset and the Muslims changed routes.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في علي بن أبي طالب وأصحابه، وذلك أنهم كانوا يمرون كل يوم على المنافقين واليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being addressed is al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad; striving to his Lord means exerting himself toward Him and meeting Him with his deeds.
rows.anchor: يعني بالإنسان الأسود بن عبد الأسد { إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا } إنك ساع إلى ربك سعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person given his book in his right hand is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, known as Abū Salama.
rows.anchor: وهو عبدالله بن عبد الأسد، ويكنى أبا سلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An easy accounting means God does not change the person’s good deeds or expose him.
rows.anchor: يقول: باليسير، بأن الله لا يغير حسناته ولا يفضحه

words: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًۭا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection, creatures surge among one another for 300 years; then the Lord sits on the Throne to judge, with the angels arrayed in ranks, and they see Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: فإنهم يموج بعضهم في بعض، مقدار ثلاث مائة سنة، حتى إذا استوى الرب جل وعز على كرسيه ليحاسب خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is brought from a distance of 500 years, held back from the creatures by 90,000 reins with 70,000 angels on each; each angel’s neck and height span a year, and the distance between his shoulders is fifty years. Their faces are like embers, their eyes like lightning, flames escape their mouths, and each carries a hammer with 360 mountain-like heads that is lighter than a feather.
rows.anchor: ويجاء بالنار، من مسيرة خمس مائة عام، عليها تسعون ألف زمام، في كل زمام سعبون ألف ملك، متعلق يحبسونها عن الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels bring Hell until it stands to the Throne’s left; Paradise is brought like a bride to her husband and stands to its right.
rows.anchor: حتى تقام عن يسار العرش. ويجاء بالجنة يزفونها كما تزف العروس إلى زوجها، حتى تقام عن يمين العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the creatures see Hell, Paradise, their Lord, and the marvels of the angels, the Throne’s bearers, the heavens’ inhabitants, and Hell’s keepers, their voices fall silent from awe and their joints tremble.
rows.anchor: فانقطعت عند ذلك أصواتهم، فلا يتكلم أحد منهم من فرق الله وعظمته، ولما يرون من العجائب من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God sees His allies’ fear and their hearts reach their throats, a caller from the Throne’s right says, “Servants, you will have no fear today, nor will you grieve”; humans and jinn, believers and unbelievers, raise their heads because all are His servants. The excerpt then introduces a second call.
rows.anchor: فيقوم مناد عن يمين العرش، فينادى: يعباد لا خوف عليكم اليوم ولا أنتم تحزنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil connects this scene to the speaker in al-Ḥāqqa 25–28, who wishes death and rest from the trial and laments that his argument has failed; the one receiving his book behind his back calls for destruction and enters the Fire.
rows.anchor: [الحاقة: 25- 28]. يقول: يا ليت كان الموت أن أموت فاستريح من هذا البلاء هلك عن حجتي اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls out in woe and enters the Fire.
rows.anchor: يقول: يدعو بالويل، ويدخل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being happy among his family means being honored among his people; God will humble him on the Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: يقول في قومه كريما، قال فيذله الله عز وجل يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thought that God would not resurrect him.
rows.anchor: يقول: أن لن يبعث الله تعالى

words: بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His Lord is the One who created him and is witness to his deeds.
rows.anchor: يقول: الذي خلقه { به بصيرا } [آية: 15] إنه شهيد لعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath invokes the sky and the Tariq; the bright, piercing star explains what the Tariq is.
rows.anchor: ما الطارق } [آية: 2] فسرها له؟ فقال: { النجم الثاقب } [آية: 3] يعني المضىء

words: إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul has angel guardians who record its good and bad deeds. God created three kinds of stars: guides for navigation, missiles against devils, and lights for the earth, and swears by them.
rows.anchor: خلق النجوم ثلاثة نجوم يهتدى بها، ونجوم رجوم للشياطين، ونجوم مصابيح الأرض، فأقسم الله عز وجل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person does not believe in resurrection, he should consider what he was created from.
rows.anchor: فإن لا يصدق هذا الإنسان بالبعث { فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gushing water is the fluids of the man and woman, which adhere to one another and form the human.
rows.anchor: خلق من ماء الرجل، والمرأة والتصق بعضه على بعض فخلق منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fluid comes between the man’s backbone and the woman’s collarbone area; tarāʾib is the place of a necklace. The man’s white, thick fluid produces nerves and bones, while the woman’s yellow, thin fluid produces flesh, blood, and hair.
rows.anchor: يقول: من بين صلب الرجل وترائب المرأة، والترائب موضع القلادة، فأما ماء الرجل، فإنه أبيض غليظ منه العصب والعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is able to resurrect the human on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قادر على أن يبعثه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden matters are tested: every secret sin committed by the child of Adam is exposed.
rows.anchor: يوم تختبر السرائر كل سريرة من الذنوب عملها ابن آدم

words: فما له من قوة ولا ناصر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person has no power to protect himself from God and no helper to rescue him from God.
rows.anchor: يمتنع من الله بقوته { ولا } له { ناصر } [آية: 10] ينصره من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s “return” means rain.
rows.anchor: ذات المطر { والأرض ذات الصدع }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s splitting means the growth of plants.
rows.anchor: والأرض ذات الصدع } [آية: 12] بالنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the sūra describes is a decisive word, meaning the true word.
rows.anchor: إن الذي وصفته في هذه السورة لقول فصل، يقول لهو قول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is not play or jest.
rows.anchor: يقول: وما هو باللعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Muhammad publicly declared faith and ʿUmar became Muslim, Quraysh feared Muhammad’s growing support and their own decline, including the risk that he would overpower them and drive them from their land. At the House of Assembly, ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa, Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, Abū al-Bakhtarī ibn Hishām, and ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī met; Satan joined in an old man’s guise, claiming to be an outsider from al-Azd (said to be from Yemen or Najd) traveling to Iraq, and they admitted him. Abū Jahl asked how to deal with Muhammad, who opposed their religion, insulted their idols, and gained followers; ʿAmr proposed putting him on a camel and expelling him from the sanctuary so his harm would fall elsewhere.
rows.anchor: فلما آمن عمر، قال بعضهم لبعض: ما ترى أمر محمد إلا يزداد يوما بيوم، ونحن في نقصان لاشك
